en.name: Gregory XV
en.summary: A reform-minded pope who founded the Vatican's missionary arm, Propaganda Fide, and introduced secret-ballot voting for papal conclaves.
en.body: Alessandro Ludovisi established the Congregation for the Propagation of the Faith in 1622 to coordinate and professionalize Catholic missionary work worldwide, an institution that endures in reorganized form to this day. He also reformed conclave procedure to require secret written ballots, reducing opportunities for coercion and vote-buying in papal elections, and canonized several major Counter-Reformation figures including Ignatius of Loyola, Francis Xavier, and Teresa of Ávila.
